**Ch 304 · day 404, the ninth of Wolfmonth, a Saturday, and not a market day in a county with a market · the mill, the gates, the glass works, the road, the lane.** A man at a mill wheel has not left it since before the water came and has come out into the cold four times for about four minutes each. **The road is four hundred yards long, made by hand in a wet summer by a man of thirty-four with sixteen men and no work, it has a crown and a ditch and a standing finish on the end of it, and it is the only straight thing in that valley and it goes nowhere, and nobody has ever asked it whether it goes anywhere.** There are three gates, and the number of crossings in a season is the one figure in that place anybody can check, and it is a figure about carts. **The word for the forgetting is said once, in a glass works, by a man with his hands in a cooling box, and it is a trade word and it is not explained and it has not been said again.** The woman with the slate loses a name in a yard at the fourth hour and has it back inside about a minute and a quarter, and the man she was writing it for does not notice. **And at the seventh hour a man of about sixty who keeps the roll of the crossing fills in nine ruled days that had been empty in the roll of everybody, and nobody asked him to, and he took about four minutes.** **Change:** **a roll with a gap in it is a roll that can be filled in, and that valley found that out on an evening in that month without anybody deciding that they had found it out, and the finding is about a piece of paper and not about a fever.** **Ends:** there is no column on that sheet for a name that got there by accident and none for one that got there on purpose, and the two are the same line in the same hand and nobody in that valley can tell them apart and never will.

**Ch 305 · day 409, the fourteenth of Wolfmonth, a Thursday and a market day · a long room at the top of a lane, eleven chairs down each long side, a clerk whose ink pot is shut nine times a week.** The room sits four days out of seven and nine people take a chair out of twenty-two and the clerk's ink pot is the only speed in the room. **A man of about sixty proposes a third book, out of his own half of the record, to be sent to a man at a stone two hundred miles off who will not read it, and his reason is his own and it is correct.** **The keeper of the roll says the fear, and the fear is correct, and it is about a copy and not about the Crown: a copy does not get anything out of the sheet and does not put anything in, and after about two years the sheet is what anybody in that valley knows about the two of them, and the two of them are still there.** The clerk reads that part of the minute back once and only once. **A woman of about thirty with the slate says the thing the volume is about, in eleven words, and no figure is printed on it: *A copy of a person is a person who was there.*** Nobody improved on it. **The room splits five and four, and the clerk writes both numbers on one line under a head of his own invention, and does not enter a reason, and that is the only thing that room has ever recorded about itself.** A man of thirty-four comes in with sixteen men and no work and gets nothing, and the true sentence anybody has said in that room in eleven years gets no answer at all. **Change:** the copy is made anyway, out of his own half, and goes into a press in a room over a cross, and the room's vote does not reach a man's own book. **Ends:** the sheet in the press will be the one that gets picked up, and it is in a room over a cross, and there is no column on either of the two of them for which of them was written by the man whose name is not on either.

**Ch 306 · day 414, the nineteenth of Wolfmonth, a Tuesday, and not a market day · the wharf, the glass works, the lane of nine doors, the box at the low gate, and the ordinary post.** A bell of nine stone goes at the fourth hour over the street at the low gate and nobody in that city has been able to account for it and nobody is going to be asked, and it is rung by whoever is nearest. **On about two hundred yards of street with about nine doors, about nine people are asked the ordinary question and about two of the nine take about a minute and a quarter over it and neither of the two mentions it.** **A man of thirty-four with sixteen men and no work says the volume's fear out loud to a stranger in a yard, once, and it foots at thirty-six words, and the stranger does not answer it.** And at the seventh hour **a man of about sixty picks a sheet out of a box at a gate where it has stood for two months in the ordinary post, does not know what office it came from, and fills in the first column with a place and the second column with a figure under a head that says *Date*, and the figure is four hundred and four because that is the last line of his own roll and a roll is not a count.** He copies his own half of the record as well and puts it in the same bag, because a man who is going to send a figure is going to send the thing the figure came from. **Change:** the copy and the sheet go out on an ordinary round at the ninth hour. **Ends:** nobody in that city knew it had ever arrived, and about two hundred of the ninth generation in that place are the only people in it who have never once been asked whether they are all right.

**Ch 307 · day 418, the twenty-third of Wolfmonth, a Saturday and a market day · a lane, a wagon arch, a door on a lane, two rooms over a weigh-house.** A courier is not a carrier and the whole difference between them is in what a man is allowed to ask either. **He comes the length of the lane, stops at the one door in it with anything cut into it, and puts a sheet on a table, and the sheet says a return is wanted, and it is a sheet of that office's own printed series with a set of market towns in the first column and a figure of persons in the second under a head that says *Date*, and the figure is about nine hundred more than the keeper would have said, and nowhere on the whole of it is the name of a person.** The keeper of records does not ask him for a name and he gives none, and when she asks who it is from he says it is for her and she tells him she did not ask that. **A second copyist of about thirty comes down three steps and says then what do we do, and the answer is nothing, and the reason is given in the plain way once and is about two hundred miles and a figure nobody knows the count of.** A woman of about thirty with a pail says one thing at each of nine doors and moves on before the knuckle has finished ringing in the frame, and the three things she says that morning are a courier, a tide and a market. A second keeper of twenty-six comes through the room and does not stop at the table. **The office pays fourpence a year and the two rooms are the salt merchant's at two shillings a month each, and the two are named together and not added.** **Change:** the sheet goes into a press that anybody can be served with, in a room whose only record of anybody who has ever come up that lane is a day-book nothing can be served out of. **Ends:** it stands at nine entries of a thing nobody asked, and there is not going to be a tenth, and a tenth would not be a gift if it came.

**Ch 308 · day 423, the twenty-eighth of Wolfmonth, a Thursday and a market day · a reach, a market street, a long room over a wharf, a yard, a room over a weigh-house.** About forty men on the reach with the road open over it and the salt over the first bay, and a man of fifty and a half laying one finish over another on the second bay with a bar he is not using. **He counts load points into a book that does not exist, about forty mornings a month, and there is a half tile under a pound in his coat and the palm of his left hand is warm at the fourth hour and about four people in that town have seen him lay it flat and not one of them has ever said so.** **The long room over the wharf is open and nobody is in it, and the bench sits on Saturdays and on nothing else in the week and this is a Thursday, and he goes up the outside stair and stands in four feet of bare floor for about as long as it takes to count nine things twice.** Under that stair is a page about nine inches by six with a figure at the top of it and nine marks under it, four of them sitting lower on the page than the other four, and **nobody has ever entered that count on a form and a count of askings is not a price and is not a count of persons and is added to nothing.** In the yard a boy of fifteen has been copying the empty space under a number for about two years and nobody has told him what goes in it, and a man of about nineteen has watched him do it four times this week. **At the eighth hour a second copyist of about thirty takes the form out of the press and puts it face up on the table in the plain way, in the hope of a person, and nobody comes, and at the ninth hour and a quarter she puts it back and does not open the day-book.** **Change:** nothing happens and the block's cost is that a woman who has wanted a line in the day-book with her own name on it since the summer before last laid a thing where a person would see it and there was not a person. **Ends:** a form went back into a press that nobody read between the eighth hour and the ninth hour and a quarter.

**Ch 309 · day 427, the second of Frostmonth, a Monday, and not a market day · a press room on the ground floor, and a room one floor up with a stove in it that is not lit.** The building turns out something near four hundred of its forms a month into nine counties and four hundred and nine parish rolls, six spaces, five heads, the sixth the same width with nothing at the top, about four of the six ruled for a figure and one for a person and not one for a person declining to be a person. The man at the stone is about fifty and has stood at a press there for thirty-one years and about eleven thousand forms have gone through his hands. **At the fourth hour he looks at a drawer and does not open it, and a boy of nineteen who set the word in it once is not in that press room and has not been in it since the second month of this year, and about two people in that building have noticed that a bench he used to be at is empty.** **Nine sheets go out, and the first column of one of the nine is not empty, and there is a space in that column about the width of a word in front of the name of the place, and on eight of the nine it is empty. Nobody saw it go in. The hand is not the press's and it is not the hand of the man of the stone, and it is smaller than a hand of fifty and steadier than a hand of nineteen, and there are about two hundred people in that building who fill in forms every day for offices that are not this one.** The man of about fifty sees it, says nothing, puts the sheet with the other eight, and **a man of about thirty who keeps that room's books says nothing about it on the way past, and the man of about sixty with a tray says his one sentence and goes out again.** A carrier of about thirty-one takes the nine down to a cart and does not read a word of them. **Change:** one of nine sheets leaves that building with a word in the space in front of the name of the place that was not struck again in the second month of this year and will not be struck again. **Ends:** it is on its way to a door in one county of nine, and a county two hundred miles from that building is on the same series, and there is no line on the whole of any of them for the name of the person whose hand it is.

**Ch 310 · day 430, the fifth of Frostmonth, a Thursday and a market day · the room over the weigh-house, a reach, a lane, a yard, a barrier hut, and a lane a mile off with a ladder against a wall.** The market, a waggon of salt, nine lines in a book that a man keeps in a lane. Forty men on a reach, nine men in a yard, a man of about fifty-five turning three bars down and up at a barrier and saying four words nobody in that county has ever asked him about. **A ladder has been standing against a wall in a lane about a mile off since a week in the middle of that autumn and nobody in that town knows it is there, and the man with the limp looks at it for about as long as it takes to look at nine feet of nothing and does not stop.** At the fourth hour the keeper of records takes a sheet out of a press and reads it in about a minute and a half. **It is a second sheet of the same series against the same set of market towns and the second column is a count of people and it is about nine hundred more than the woman holding the sheet would have said, and the first one gave a day by which cause might be shown to an office two hundred miles off and about four days of that day are left and nobody in that town knows there is a day, and nobody in that county has been asked to show cause and is not going to be asked.** The answer is nothing, said once, and the instrument for nothing is a day-book nine entries long that nothing in this kingdom can be served out of, and a tenth is not coming and would not be a gift. **And at the seventh hour a carter of about thirty-four with a load of lime asks what a cart costs to take a load two hundred miles, and there is no rate in that county and there never has been one, and the ordinary way that room answers a question it cannot answer is with a piece of paper, and she gives him a sheet of the printed series with a head over the first column and a head over the second, and he puts it in his coat, and it goes in a bag on an ordinary round.** The account foots at eight pence and the fourpence a year and the two shillings a month are named after the total and are not added. **Change:** a carter leaves a county with a form in his coat because he asked a question with no answer in it. **Ends:** not a man and not a city — a ladder in a lane a mile off, a county with two crossings in it that the county says are four hundred yards apart, a bell that went at the fourth hour and a half as it does, nine lines in a book nobody can be served out of, and a form in a bag.

### The ten endings, as a list

1. **301, discovery** — a man who keeps a roll of four hundred people says *I do not know* about nine ruled days in it, and it is the first time anybody in that valley has been told in words that they are not known, and it was told to a stranger on the day he came.
2. **302, cost** — a roll with a column for a day and a name and a mark and no column for the day a person goes, and a man entered in it who cannot get out of it by leaving.
3. **303, discovery** — there is a roll of who is in a valley and there has never been a roll of who is known to whom, and nobody in that city can be told which of the two they would have to be asked for.
4. **304, reversal** — a roll with a gap in it is a roll that can be filled in, and nobody in that valley can tell a name that got there by accident from one that got there on purpose, and never will.
5. **305, cost** — the sheet in the press will be the one that gets picked up, and there is no column on either of the two of them for which of them was written by the man whose name is not on either.
6. **306, earned hook** — a copy of nine hundred lines and a printed sheet go out on an ordinary round at the ninth hour, and nobody in that city knew the sheet had ever arrived.
7. **307, cost** — a day-book that nothing in the world can be served out of stands at nine entries of a thing nobody asked, and a tenth is not coming and would not be a gift.
8. **308, cost** — a form goes back into a press that nobody read between the eighth hour and the ninth hour and a quarter.
9. **309, discovery** — one of nine sheets has something in the space in front of the name of the place, in a hand that is not the press's, and there is no line on the whole of it for the person whose hand it is.
10. **310, cost** — not a man and not a city: a ladder, two crossings four hundred yards apart, a bell going as it does, nine lines in a book nobody can be served out of, and a form in a carter's coat going two hundred miles in a bag on an ordinary round.

### What the block did not do, one line each

It printed no fifth unattributed two-line statement and its one full-line italic is the money footing. It printed no word in front of a place name and defined nothing and struck no type. It mentioned no tile on a coping. It named, measured, ruled across, pointed at and used neither line in a stone, and it called neither a seam, and it named one crossing and not the other. It dug for no hemp and asked whether it was there. It reconciled no refusal figures and added no two of them and added none to a figure of persons. It added no doors to doors and worked out no total and said no county. It put the two crossings in no book and in no sentence by anybody. It entered no tenth not-asking and repaired no breach, and the day-book was not opened on any day of the block. It put no two people on a road together, and all ten chapters carry the nobody-walked line. It did not spend the magistrate's construction. It did not ask the man of forty-seven a sixth time. It did not move the count of nine and did not seat the bench. It did not thank the woman of thirty-three, who is not on the page. It did not print the marginal instruction's nine words. It printed no count of the looks at the leaf. It explained no mechanism and printed no System panel. It merged no proceedings and put no delegation in a room. It added no enemy, office, council, order or mechanism. It did not name the antagonist. It did not put a member of the Culling Order on a page.

## Volume 07 Batch 0002 — Chapters 311–320, "What a Copy Is For"

**The block.** Main world and path time, day 431, the sixth of Frostmonth, YR 316, a Friday and not a market day, to day 470, the fifteenth of Hearthmonth, YR 316, a Tuesday and not a market day and the block's last day. Forty days in the block. Two market mornings printed, and eleven market days in the block on the chain. **23,643 words in ten chapters.** The frame is counted from `outline/volume-07.md` §17 and not from the prompt, and all ten datelines are exact, and **the prompt's Chapter 317 card gives day 461 as a Friday and the chain and §17 and the page all give a Sunday, and the page follows the chain.** No bench sat in this block. The bell did not go in this block. Nothing in this block is sent to the city four hundred miles off behind the reader, and the path is on the page once, in Chapter 316, and no month name and no weekday is spoken in its body.

### The ten chapters

**Ch 311 · day 431, the sixth of Frostmonth, a Friday, and not a market day · the room over a weigh-house with a door on a lane, and the lane, and the tide.** The tide has been under the boards of the lower room about thirty hours and nobody has swept it. A press that anybody who walks up that lane can be served with, a shelf with about four hundred bundles on it, and a second press four hundred yards up the county's own road that nothing can be served out of. **A register with five entries, all questions, none a finding, all opening with a set of market towns, the fifth dated and about four months old, and a day-book with nine entries of a thing that was not asked that no hand in this kingdom can be served out of.** The keeper of records is twenty-nine on a deed of thirteen words at fourpence a year. **At about the second hour she begins a proposal: that this office keep a copy of every question put to this county and give a copy to anybody who asks one. She writes it on that office's own printed series because there is no other series, and the first mistake is in the first line of it, a figure of persons into the second column under a head that says *Date*, and she knew that when she sent it.** She says it out loud in the room, which is the first time in four years and a half she has said anything about a sheet there. She puts *keeper of records* in the fifth column, which is the only column on the whole of that series that will take a person, and it will not take a name. **The reeve, the elder sister of the magistrate, who has not voted on the guild's own matter in nine years, comes up the lane with a tally, reads it standing up, and refuses, and the reason is that a copy of what it has been asked is the first thing that makes a county a thing anybody can act on, and this room will not be the place it happens in, and she did not vote on it this morning either, and she did not vote on it any morning for nine years.** Nobody improved on it. The refusal goes into the register and the register takes it as a question, because a body corporate with a door and a number can be sued for a finding and not for a question, and the register stands at six. **A sweep of the lane, a waggon of lime that cannot be weighed because the scale has not been used since the fourth of a month, and a money column of five items footed in pence at nine pence on the page, with the fourpence a year and the salt merchant's two shillings a month named outside the chain and never added.** **Ends (cost):** a register with six entries in it, every one a question, and the office that would keep a copy of what this county is asked is the office that cannot answer any of the six, and there is no line in that register for a refusal and there never has been one, and a woman wrote down a true thing in the wrong column on purpose and sent it two hundred miles and will do it again in about a month because there is nothing else to write it on.

**Ch 312 · day 436, the eleventh of Frostmonth, a Wednesday, and not a market day · the same room, and a fair copy, and a day-book nobody can open.** The tide has gone back and the lower room is dry for the first time in a month and a woman with a pail swept it on the Monday, which is the only time in four years and a half anybody in that county has swept it. **A fair copy of the register is begun at about the second hour by the second copyist of about thirty, six years in that room, and finished at about the fourth hour and a half, and nobody asked for it and it is the first fair copy that office has made in four years and a half.** **A fair copy in that county carries the person by what she does and has never carried a name, and she puts her trade at the foot of it, and about four people in that lane have worked out that a woman who has wanted a line in a day-book with her own name on it since the summer before last has just got the opposite of it, on a book anybody who walks up that lane can be served out of, and she said why before anybody worked it out.** **She then says the true thing about the day-book: it cannot be copied, because a not-asking is not a place and not a figure and not a person and not a keeper and not a frequency, and the sixth column has no head and a column with no head is not a column, and nobody improved on it.** The fair copy goes on the shelf and not into the press, and the copyist points out that they have just made a thing that can be produced out of the one thing in that room that could not be produced. On the reach the man of fifty and a half is spreading a second finish over a first one, and the fourth bay took a third day to point, and about four hundred yards of lane is a lane a carter said he wanted a price for in the last volume and got a column. **Ends (cost):** a fair copy of a register of six questions and no finding on a shelf, with a line at the foot of it that has a person at the end of it and no name, and the day-book not opened, and no tenth, and a tenth would not be a gift if it came.

**Ch 313 · day 441, the sixteenth of Frostmonth, a Monday, and not a market day · a building of four floors and seven presses, a chamber on the third floor with no window, and a vestry behind the choir of a church four hundred yards from the front of it.** A woman of thirty-eight has been in that building nine years and what she has at the end of every one of the nine is a figure, and a figure fits in one hand. She came up that stair out of a chamber with a register nineteen years old that takes a proceeding as a line, in which nine proceedings are entered and every one of the nine is a figure and not one is a question and there is no line in it for what anybody was asked. **In the spring a witness performed the best possible version of what she wants in front of her in a chamber, in eleven sentences, and it did not work, and the space after the eleventh stroke in that minute is ruled and empty.** She passes a man of about fifty at a stone in the same passage twice a month and neither of them ever says a word. **At about the fourth hour she goes down a street into a church and through to a vestry, and a churchwarden of about fifty with an eleven-year minute book refuses her, and his reason is his own and is not about her: a question in that book is read out in that church once a year in front of about four hundred people, and a parish that cannot answer a thing is a parish that is asked it again, and the rate is settled at the quarter-day and comes back to him on that morning.** She puts her want down once. Nobody improved on anything. **And then he asks her a question — what the figure under the head that says a day is a count of — and she cannot answer it, and about four seconds of that vestry are on the page, and the ordinary question is the only question anybody in this kingdom has ever asked about a figure on that series, and it has been answered once, in a county two hundred miles off, by a man who is not in that room.** The refusal is entered in his own hand in about four seconds and not read again. Nobody thanked her for asking or for being answered and nobody told her she was right, and the aphorism that being correct is the most expensive thing available to a person in a chamber is printed once here and nowhere else in the block. **And the keeper of records of a body corporate two hundred miles off is not told any of it and is not the instrument this woman works for, and no paper in either office would carry a word of the morning to the other, and nobody in either has ever been in the other's room.** **Ends (cost):** a man of about fifty has shut a minute book and gone out into a churchyard, and one of the two of them has been refused the only thing she has asked for in nine years and the other did not know it had happened until she stood in front of him, and neither has said a word about the other's morning, and there is a drawer in that vestry with a sheet of a printed series in it that nobody has ever done anything with.

**Ch 314 · day 446, the twenty-first of Frostmonth, a Saturday and a market day · a market four hundred yards long, about four hundred people in it, a reach, a yard, a barrier hut, a woman with a pail, and a long room over a wharf with its outside stair standing open and nobody on it.** The market is on from the second hour to about the seventh and a waggon of the salt merchant's salt stands at the mouth of the channel road with nobody under it. **A long room over a wharf at the north end of that market is open, and a bench of nine sits in it on Saturdays and on nothing else in the week at about the seventh hour, and this day has not got to the seventh hour, and so nobody went up that stair, and the last person up it was a man of thirty-two with a limp on the Wednesday before last who stood on four bare feet of floor between the table and the wall for about as long as nine things take to count twice and did not go a step further.** Under that stair is a page about nine inches by six with a figure at the top of it and nine marks under it, five low and four high, and nobody has ever entered that count on a form. The reach is going with about forty men on it, the road open, the salt over the first bay, a man of fifty and a half on the second bay with a bar he is not using who argues with the man with the limp about whether a book and a deck are the same thing, and **the whole of what that man is for in this county is a tally he keeps on the timber which has no number on it, belongs to no office, cannot be produced by anybody and is not on a form, and the palm of his left hand is warm at about the fourth hour and has been for two years and four people have watched him lay it on cold timber and not one of them has ever said a word.** In the yard four hundred yards up the county's own road a boy of fifteen copies the widest of the four spaces on a board as well as the numbers and nobody has ever told him what goes in a space, a man of about nineteen with an empty hod watches him do it, and the man of twenty-five who owns that yard says he will say where it is once more and then not again. A man of about sixty keeps a lime heap tight against a wall under a lid with his back to the yard and is the one man there the yard does not pay. ### The ten endings, as a list

1. **311, cost** — a register with six entries in it, every one a question, and the office that would keep a copy of what this county is asked is the office that cannot answer any of the six, and there is no line in that register for a refusal and there never has been one.
2. **312, cost** — a fair copy with a line at the foot of it that has a person at the end of it and no name, on a shelf, in a room with a day-book that cannot be copied and was not opened.
3. **313, cost** — two people four hundred yards apart, each of whom has said one reason and neither of whom has ever said the other's out loud, and a drawer with a sheet in it that nobody has ever done anything with.
4. **314, cost** — a bench sat at about the seventh hour with nothing to be put in front of it, and a page under a stair that says nine, and nobody in that county has ever been asked to move it and nobody is going to be.
5. **315, cost** — a page under a stair says nine and there is no second of it in this kingdom, and the whole of why there is not is that nobody has ever been told it is there.
6. **316, cost** — two books of nine spreads six feet apart in a room over a cross, one made by the man who keeps it and one by a man who does not, and no line in that room says which of them is the one that happened.
7. **317, discovery** — a place with nothing against it came round nine counties and came back, and nobody in that county was told that the two things are the same kind of thing.
8. **318, discovery** — a book with a person at the front of every one of its eleven lines, not on the office's series, in a room nobody two floors up has ever been asked to see, and the answer to what that office's sheets are for is that room.
9. **319, cost** — a day went, a day-book did not open, and the two people in that county who knew the day was there are four hundred yards apart and have never spoken about it.
10. **320, cost** — two women two hundred miles apart, neither the other's instrument, and a sheet about nine inches by six under a stair that says nine, and nobody in that county has ever been asked to move it.

### The card, with every deviation counted and judged

1. **The prompt's Chapter 317 card gives day 461 as a Friday. The chain counted forward from day 390 and §17's own row for day 466 both give the sixth of Hearthmonth, YR 316, as a Sunday, and the page is a Sunday.** **Judged: the outline and the chain govern, and the prompt is wrong in one weekday, and the chapter is a Sunday, and the chapter's two other Sundays' consequences were checked against the county's two market days and there is no collision.**
2. **The prompt's Chapter 312 card puts two people with an instrument and has not used it in two rooms four hundred miles apart. The fen county and the provincial town are two hundred miles apart on eleven datelines since the Batch 0001 repair, and no Volume 07 chapter may print a hundred and forty for that distance.** **Judged: two hundred, and the page says two hundred, and the two people are the second copyist of about thirty and a Crown officer of thirty-eight in two rooms two hundred miles apart, and the block does not put them in one room.**
3. **The prompt's Chapter 315 card places the man of about fifty-five and a roll of a hundred and forty askings in a valley four hundred miles off. Canon puts a man of about fifty-five at a barrier of three bars in the fen county and puts the hundred and forty cut into the end of a bench in a room over a cross four hundred miles off, and no person keeps it.** **Judged: the page follows canon. The man of fifty-five is the barrier man of Chapter 310 and Chapter 314, and the hundred and forty is not on Chapter 315's page at all and is not reconciled with anything, and the fear is stated by the clerk of about sixty, who is one of the four people in this kingdom with an instrument they have not used, which is the shape the prompt's card asks for.**
4. **The prompt's Chapter 314 card gives a long room over a wharf with the bench not sitting because this is a Saturday and the bench sits on Saturdays. That is not a reason and the requirement against seating the bench is absolute.** **Judged: the reason on the page is the hour. The chapter's hours are the second, the fourth and the fifth, the market closes at about the seventh, and a bench of nine sits at about the seventh, and the chapter ends before the sitting. The bench is not seated, the count under the stair does not move, and the volume's one bench sitting remains Block 0005's day 551.**
5. **The prompt's Chapter 312 card and `outline/volume-07.md` §13 both place the man of thirty-four's thirty-six-word want in Batch 0002, and Batch 0001 printed it and footed it at thirty-six.** **Judged: not reprinted, no length figure on it, not improved on, and the figure `thirty-six` is at zero across the ten new files, and Chapter 316's man of thirty-four says other things and none of them is that.**
6. **`outline/volume-07.md` §13 assigns Batch 0002's one name slot to a person of about forty on a path's council of nine who has taken the cure, and the cure is Batch 0003's beat.** **Judged: the block spent no name and the reason is that a slot spent on a face whose only function is to be corrected in the next block is a slot spent on a scene. The two names already in the volume are printed once and twice as returns.**
7. **The block's `about` per-chapter column is 13.10 / 15.57 / 20.84 / 16.11 / 22.20 / 20.54 / 18.50 / 24.93 / 26.25 / 18.52, and Batch 0001's split of low-labour and high-document chapters does not reproduce.** **Judged: the block is eight document rooms and two labour days, and Chapter 311 is a document chapter with a long ordinary frame around it and Chapter 314 is a labour chapter with a room at both ends of it, and the split is a fact about the block's shape and not a defect. The block mean of 19.30 is inside the 18 to 22 band and that is the figure the band is about.**
8. **The block's two reporting devices came out of a first pass at 54 for *about four people* and 39 for *have said since that*, against targets of about 21 and about 26.** **Judged: twenty-three and twenty-seven on the page, and the reduction was made by converting reporting clauses and not by deleting a single one, and the reduction is a device change and not a content change.**
9. **The clause-level sweep on the basis the previous blocks used returned 2,437 hits on a containment reading, which is useless, and fifty on a Jaccard reading, and the raw-token reading returned 304 runs of fifteen words or more with a longest of sixty-seven.** **Judged: all fifty re-voiced and the Jaccard reading now returns zero, and every run above twenty-five words was re-voiced and the longest is now twenty-three and the twenty-three are the house dateline formula. This is the sixth block in a row on which a basis this project has written down returned clean on a real defect, and the first block in which the defect was found by a writer and not by a reviewer, and the standing lesson is unchanged: a report of a sweep has to name the basis it ran on, and the basis has to be recorded before the run and not after it.**
10. **A drafting note was left in the body of Chapter 312** — a line of the writer's own reasoning about a token and a provincial town — **and it was found on the page before the last sweep and is gone.** Judged: a defect of the same class the review over Batch 0001 found, and it is recorded because a reader of the ten chapters needs to know it was there.

### What the block did not do, one line each

It printed no fifth unattributed two-line statement, and its two full-line italics are the money footings in Chapters 311 and 320. It printed no word in front of a place name, defined nothing and struck no type, and the type case in the provincial town was not looked at in this block. It did not identify the hand on the one of nine sheets and did not have anybody find out. It mentioned no tile on a coping and scheduled nothing for it. It named, measured, ruled across, pointed at and used neither line in a stone and called neither of them a seam, and it named no crossing at all in this block, and the two crossings are not in one sentence by anybody. It dug for no hemp and asked whether it was there, and the one `hemp` on the page is a winter book's binding. It reconciled no refusal figures, added no two of them and added none to a figure of persons, and the count of askings on a page under a stair is nine and did not move. It added about four hundred doors to about four hundred doors, worked out no total, said no county for any list, and **the carrier of about fifty with a firm of two is not on the page in any construction, not even as an absence.** It entered no tenth not-asking and repaired no breach, and the day-book was not opened on any day in the block. It put no two people on a road together, and all ten chapters carry the nobody-walked line. It did not spend the magistrate's construction, did not have her use it and did not have anybody write it down for her, and **she is not on the page in this block at all.** It did not ask the man of forty-seven a sixth time, did not get him the four things a sixth time, and **it did not ask the man of about fifty-five where his four words come from and did not print them.** It did not enter a tenth asking of the bench and **did not seat the bench in any chapter, because the block's Chapter 314 is a Saturday whose hours end before the seventh hour and no chapter in the block puts nine men on that bench.** It did not thank the woman of thirty-three, convert her, change her want or turn her leaf over, **and she is not on the page in this block at all.** It did not print the marginal instruction's nine words and did not print the woman's own nine words, which are spent. It printed no count of the looks at a leaf and he does not take the leaf out in either chapter he is in it in this block. It **did not reprint the man of thirty-four's thirty-six words, did not reprint the volume's sixteen-word sentence, and put no length figure on either.** It did not re-enter the one finding in the winter book, did not ask anybody about it, and did not reprint the four lines at the head of the first spread. It explained no mechanism and printed no System panel. It merged no proceedings and put no delegation in a room. It added no enemy, office, council, order or mechanism, and every person who acts on a sheet in this block has a want that has nothing to do with this book. It did not name the antagonist. It did not put a member of the Culling Order on a page, and it printed the phrase zero times. **The bell did not go in this block, and one instance of it was written into Chapter 320's last paragraph in drafting and taken out before the last sweep.**
